editorial:
Imagine living in a place where karate isn't just a sport, but the actual law of the land. That is the wild world you enter here, where you follow Bobby, a lonely kid who just wants to fit in. Things get really weird when he starts seeing the ghost of Johnny Maim, who was his dad's favorite action movie star from back in the day. The vibe is a great mix of silly humor and heart, feeling like those classic 80s movies where a misfit finds a mentor in the strangest way possible. It is less about serious fighting and more about a kid finding his own confidence with a loud, ghostly movie star shouting tips in his ear.

The action scenes are snappy and the comedy hits just right, though some of the plot twists are a bit predictable. You will love the chemistry between the living and the dead, which keeps the energy high throughout. If you are looking for a fun night in, you should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the flashy fight effects. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move for the bonus features. It is a perfect pick for a family movie night or anyone who needs a good laugh.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Bobby realizes that Johnny Maim is not just teaching him how to fight, but how to be brave. Bobby wins the big tournament by using a move that is totally his own, rather than just copying Johnny. This success allows Johnny to finally let go of his ego and move on to the afterlife. The movie ends with Bobby becoming a leader in his town, proving that heart matters more than strict rules.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy action movies and underdog stories.
